confirmed.title: Invoice match uses actual receipt quantity, not the recognized line contribution, so excess receipts are billed as MATCHED/SATISFIED
confirmed.failure_scenario: This is the D13 '60+40/excess 5' fixture with invoices added. PO line is 100 BOX @1 EUR. Receipt R1 is 60 (credited 60). Receipt R2 is 45: creditReceipt credits 40 and records excess 5 under PURCHASE_EXCESS_RECONCILIATION. The supplier invoices I1 = 60 BOX / 60 EUR against R1 and I2 = 45 BOX / 45 EUR against R2. matchInvoice(I2) reads received = actualQuantity 45 and ordered = 100, so quantity = 45, expected = 45, qd = pd = diff = 0. prior is 0 because R2 is a different reference. Result: status MATCHED, settlementResult SATISFIED, no SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty. The line is invoiced 105 against an order of 100, and the 5 excess boxes are billed with no settlement difference. A MANAGER can then waive the excess-receipt duty, and the overbilling is recorded nowhere.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementTradeFacts.java:8 documents 'quantity is currently recognized real contribution'. The adapter returns "quantity" = credit.actualQuantity (line 37 for PURCHASE, line 34 for SALE). recognizedQuantity (contributedQuantity) is returned but nothing reads it. SettlementCommands.java:53 uses received = positive(contribution.get("quantity")) and caps only per contribution with received.min(ordered), where ordered is the full line quantity, not the remaining quantity. The overlap check counts only the same (line, reference, kind). PurchaseCommands.java:75-76 shows ReceiptCredits splitting actualQuantity from contributedQuantity/excessQuantity. The V27 CHECK has no cumulative per-line bound. No backend or T19 case has multi-receipt excess.
confirmed.fix: Match against the recognized contribution (contributedQuantity / legitimateQuantity). Also compute cumulative matched quantity per line and kind across all references against the ordered quantity, and set the quantity/scope difference when it is exceeded. Add a 60 + 45 (40 + 5 excess) Postgres case.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The failure path is reachable in the reviewed code. HEAD 48d616e3 has no backend diff from 6fa7beb1.

Path, step by step:
1. `PurchaseCommands.creditReceipt` (PurchaseCommands.java:76) accepts R2 = 45 against 40 remaining. It stores ReceiptCredits with actualQuantity 45, contributedQuantity 40 and excessQuantity 5, and opens PURCHASE_EXCESS_RECONCILIATION. `ReceiptCommands` (lines 58-59) adds no per-line cap.
2. `recordInvoice` (SettlementCommands.java:44-50) never compares the invoice quantity with the referenced contribution or with cumulative line invoicing.
3. `SettlementFactsAdapter.contribution` (line 37) returns `"quantity"` = credit.actualQuantity. `"recognizedQuantity"` is returned but never read. This also contradicts the interface doc at SettlementTradeFacts.java:8, which says quantity is "currently recognized real contribution".
4. In `match` (SettlementCommands.java:53), the inputs are received=45, ordered=100 (full line quantity, not remaining), iq=45, price=1. That gives quantity=45, expected=45, diff=qd=pd=0. `prior` only counts the same line, same reference and same invoiceKind, so it is 0, and overlap is 45>45, which is false. Status is MATCHED and settlementResult is SATISFIED, with no SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty.
5. The V27 Matches CHECK passes: quantity<=received/ordered/invoice, qd=iq-received=0, originalDifference=0. The V29 status CHECK is consistent with MATCHED. No trigger or constraint bounds cumulative invoicing per line.
6. `SettlementQueries` (line 19) also reports SATISFIED.

The line ends up invoiced 105 against PO 100 with no settlement difference.

The strongest sign that this is a defect and not an intended design: the single-receipt case is flagged. Receipt 105 on PO 100 with invoice 105 gives received.min(ordered)=100, expected=100 and diff=5, so DIFFERENCE. The same overbilling split across two receipts goes undetected, because `ordered` is the full line quantity rather than the remaining quantity, and `received` is the actual quantity rather than the credited contribution.

Plan requirements this breaks:
- §6 settlement: "PO line↔receipt contribution↔invoice line … 수량·가격·통화별 대조", and a settlement difference is a separate unresolved goal.
- D13: excess must not be silently folded into the order.

The s4c-settlement README defines scopeDifference only per same reference ("실제 수령/인도량") and does not address excess across references.

Test coverage does not catch it:
- `SettlementCommandPostgresTest` uses only a single receipt of 100 on PO 100.
- The T19 fixtures use purchase 100 and sale 30 with no excess.
- The native E1 `matchInvoice` case (author.py:119) tests a price/amount gap of 5, not excess.

One overstatement in the claim: the overbilling is not "recorded nowhere". The immutable ReceiptCredits.excessQuantity=5 and Match.receivedQuantity/orderedQuantity remain, and the PURCHASE_EXCESS_RECONCILIATION duty is visible while open. But the settlement outcome itself is wrong (SATISFIED, no settlement duty), so P1 (plan requirement violated and untested) stands. It is not P0, because no existing acceptance case exercises it and no stock or ledger data is corrupted.

confirmed.title: SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty resolves on zero remaining amount while the product's own settlement result still says UNSATISFIED (quantity difference ignored by the resolver)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Line ordered 100 BOX @1 EUR, receipt actual 100. Invoice claims quantity 120 @1 EUR = 120. matchInvoice: quantity=min(100,100,120)=100, expected=100, originalDifference=20, quantityDifference=20, status DIFFERENCE, SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty opened. MANAGER proposes+confirms an adjustment of 20 EUR. resolveObligation(duty, confirmedAdjustmentId): SettlementResponsibilities checks only currencyDifference/scopeDifference and remaining()==0, so the duty becomes RESOLVED. getSettlement for the same invoice computes result = remaining==0 AND quantityDifference==0 AND ... -> quantityDifference is 20 -> 'UNSATISFIED'. Outcome: a settlement that the product itself reports as unsatisfied has no open human duty, violating plan §6 '정산 차이는 별도 미해결 목표' and the V29 rule that every DIFFERENCE keeps its human duty. Existing test exactManagerConfirmationRetainsOriginalVarianceAndDuty only uses a pure price difference (qd=0), so it passes.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementResponsibilities.java:29-30 — `if(Boolean.TRUE.equals(match.get("currencyDifference"))||Boolean.TRUE.equals(match.get("scopeDifference")))throw ...; if(settlement.remaining(c,match).signum()!=0)throw ...;` (no quantityDifference check). SettlementQueries.java:19 — `settlement.put("result",remaining.signum()==0&&decimal(m.get("quantityDifference")).signum()==0&&!currencyDifference&&!scopeDifference?"SATISFIED":"UNSATISFIED")`. Test: SettlementCommandPostgresTest.java:140 (`originalDifference` 5, quantities equal).
confirmed.fix: Make the resolver and the query agree: in SettlementResponsibilities.requireResolution also throw HELD when match.quantityDifference != 0 (an amount adjustment cannot discharge an over/under-invoiced quantity), or, if the intended semantics is that a MANAGER-confirmed amount adjustment settles the quantity variance in money, change SettlementQueries.result to the same predicate as the resolver. Add a Postgres test with invoiceQuantity != receivedQuantity covering both the resolver and getSettlement.result.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. The cited code at 6fa7beb1 is byte-identical to the working tree.

**How the scenario plays out**

1. **Recording the over-quantity invoice is not blocked.**
   - `SettlementCommands.invoice` only checks that the unit matches, that quantity × price equals the amount exactly, and that the source fields match. Nothing caps the invoice quantity at the ordered or received quantity.
   - The canonical INVOICE proof is checked against the invoice's own quantity of 120 (`proof(...,"INVOICE",iq,unit)`).
   - `PurchaseCommands.recordExecutionEffect` accepts INVOICED 120 on a line ordered at 100.

2. **The match records both differences and opens the duty.**
   - With ordered 100, received 100, invoiced 120 @1, `match()` gives quantity=min(100,100,120)=100, expected=100, diff=20, qd=iq−received=20 and pd=0.
   - The status is DIFFERENCE, and the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty is opened through `impact.recorded`.

3. **A MANAGER adjustment brings the remaining amount to zero.**
   - A PROPOSE followed by a CONFIRM of amount 20 goes through `manager()`, the hash check and the policy check.
   - `remaining()` = 20 − 20 = 0.

4. **The resolver accepts it.**
   - `ResponsibilityService.settle` calls `ResponsibilityEvidenceGate`, which calls `SettlementResponsibilities.requireResolution`.
   - That method checks that the adjustment is CONFIRMED for the same invoice and match, has an approver, and has a non-superseded occurrence.
   - It rejects currencyDifference and scopeDifference, and requires `remaining == 0`.
   - It never looks at `quantityDifference`, so the duty is updated to RESOLVED with basis VERIFIED_RESOLUTION.

5. **The settlement view still says UNSATISFIED, permanently.**
   - `SettlementQueries` line 19 computes SATISFIED only when remaining==0, quantityDifference==0, no currency difference and no scope difference. Here it returns UNSATISFIED.
   - The match row is immutable: a second match is rejected with INVOICE_ALREADY_MATCHED, and the V27 trigger blocks changes.
   - CREDIT_NOTE and CORRECTION invoices cannot be matched: they are HELD by the command and rejected by a V29 trigger.
   - So once the invoice quantity differs from the received quantity, nothing can ever turn this settlement SATISFIED, yet the only duty is closed.

**Why this looks like an omission rather than a design choice**

- The resolver's predicate is the query's SATISFIED predicate with only the quantity clause removed.
- It explicitly states that currency and scope differences are "not closed by an amount adjustment". A quantity difference is the same kind of non-amount difference.
- The plan's settlement rule (§6) matches by quantity, price and currency, and treats a settlement difference as a separate unresolved goal. The plan's acceptance criteria (§13) require zero false completions (허위 완료0건).

**Test coverage**

- The only resolve test, `exactManagerConfirmationRetainsOriginalVarianceAndDuty`, uses a pure price difference (qd=0).
- The T19 `invoice-quantity-difference` subcase records and matches the invoice but never adjusts or resolves.
- So no test exercises this path.

**Corrections to the claim**

- It misreads V29. "Every DIFFERENCE keeps its human duty" is a CHECK that `dutyRootId` is not null; it does not require the duty to stay OPEN.
- It is not certain which side is wrong: either the resolver should hold, or the query should treat a MANAGER-confirmed amount adjustment as settling the quantity variance.
- Either way, the product reports two contradictory states with no owner. That is still a gap in a plan requirement (§6, §13).
- It is not P0: closing the duty takes a deliberate MANAGER confirmation, and the original variance stays readable.

Severity stays at P1.

confirmed.title: Settlement result is never re-evaluated after a delivery or receipt correction; getSettlement stays SATISFIED
confirmed.failure_scenario: Sales line is 100 @1000 KRW. Delivery 100 (legitimate 100). SALE invoice 100 / 100000 KRW is matched: MATCHED, SATISFIED, no duty. A verified delivery correction then sets actual = 98. correctionImpact opens only the logistics DELIVERY_CORRECTED_DEFICIT (2). The Match row is immutable and getSettlement derives its result from the stored match, so it still reports SATISFIED with quantityDifference 0. If a MANAGER waives the deficit ('customer accepts 98'), the 2-unit / 2000 KRW overbilling has no settlement difference and no owner.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementQueries.java:19 computes result only from stored m.quantityDifference, currencyDifference, scopeDifference and adjustments. SettlementFactsAdapter.contribution (line 34) is read only inside matchInvoice (SettlementCommands.java:53). DeliveryCorrection.correctionImpact (lines 8-12) has no settlement hook. grep finds no settlement reference in the sales, receipt or purchase packages. Plan §4.3 requires corrections to re-evaluate affected judgments and duties. §6 정산 treats the settlement difference as a separate unresolved goal.
confirmed.fix: In correctionImpact (and receipt corrections), find Matches on the corrected reference. When the current contribution differs from receivedQuantity, record an immutable settlement re-assessment and open a SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty. At minimum, make getSettlement return UNVERIFIED/UNSATISFIED when the referenced contribution has a newer correction.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute the claim. The scenario can happen in the code at the reviewed commit, and the backend has not changed between 6fa7beb1 and HEAD.

1. **The match is a frozen snapshot.** `SettlementCommands.match` (SettlementCommands.java:53-57) reads the current contribution once through `SettlementFactsAdapter.contribution` → `DeliveryCorrection.deliveryCredit`, whose `actualQuantity` is 100. It then writes an immutable Match row with `quantityDifference=0` and `originalDifference=0`, status MATCHED. Because the status is MATCHED, it opens no SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty.

2. **The query only reads that snapshot.** `SettlementQueries.query` (line 19) builds the result from the stored row's `quantityDifference`, `originalDifference`, `currencyDifference` and `scopeDifference`, plus CONFIRMED adjustments. It never calls `facts.contribution` again, so it returns SATISFIED.

3. **The correction can still happen after the invoice is matched.**
   - `EvidenceReconciliation.linkCanonicalOccurrence` calls `AssessmentCorrectionImpact.evidenceLinked` (EvidenceReconciliation.java:194), which calls `DeliveryCorrection.correctionImpact` (AssessmentCorrectionImpact.java:38-42).
   - Neither `deliveryCorrectionPrior` (EvidenceReconciliation.java:144-150) nor `correctionImpact` (DeliveryCorrection.java:8-9) checks for existing INVOICED effects or Matches.
   - `correctionImpact` inserts a DeliveryCorrections row (98), marks the work invalidated, and opens only DELIVERY_CORRECTED_DEFICIT with quantity 2. It does not touch Matches or settlement.

4. **No other code re-evaluates settlement.**
   - Outside the settlement package, settlement is referenced only by `SettlementFactsAdapter` and `ObligationClosureCatalog`. There is no correction listener and no reconciler.
   - No test corrects a delivery or receipt after a match: `DeliveryCorrectionTest`, `FulfillmentPostgresTest` and the C4 fixtures have no invoice or settlement assertions, and `SettlementCommandPostgresTest` only covers CREDIT_NOTE/CORRECTION invoices being HELD.

5. **Mitigation is partial only.**
   - If the original work is still open, the DELIVERY_CORRECTED_DEFICIT duty shows up in `getSettlement`'s `obligations` list, because it is filtered by the same workId. If that work is CLOSED, the duty goes to a follow-up work and does not show.
   - Either way, `settlement.result` stays SATISFIED with `quantityDifference` 0.
   - ObligationClosureCatalog.java:29 allows a MANAGER waiver of that logistics duty. After a waiver, invoice 100 against an actual delivery of 98 has no settlement difference and no owner.

6. **This breaks plan requirements.**
   - §4.3: a correction must re-evaluate affected judgments and duties in the same unit of work.
   - §6 정산 rule: a settlement difference is a separate unresolved goal even when the logistics goal is met.

**Severity:** P2 is fair rather than P1. The failure needs a correction to arrive after matching, no named acceptance fixture (C4 or D19) covers this combination, and the deficit duty partly exposes the problem while it is open. The claimed failure is still real: the settlement result is wrong and the difference can be left with no owner.

confirmed.title: SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE closes on amount alone: a zero-amount 'adjustment' resolves a pure quantity/price mismatch and bypasses the typed waiver
confirmed.failure_scenario: (a) Receipt is 100 BOX @1 EUR. Invoice is 50 BOX @2 EUR = 100 EUR. qd = -50, pd = +1, originalDifference = 0, so the match is DIFFERENCE with a duty. A holder of the recordSettlementAdjustment ManagementAuthority PROPOSEs and CONFIRMs a 0 EUR adjustment. remaining = 0, and resolveObligation succeeds as VERIFIED_RESOLUTION. There is no WAIVE approval, no decideQuantityDutyWaiver designation, no single-use binding, and 50 boxes stay un-invoiced. (b) T19's 'invoice 105 BOX vs receipt 100': confirming a 5 EUR adjustment marks the duty RESOLVED, but getSettlement requires quantityDifference == 0 and so reports UNSATISFIED forever, with no open duty or owner.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementResponsibilities.java:29-30 rejects only currencyDifference/scopeDifference and requires remaining(match) == 0; it ignores quantityDifference and priceDifference. SettlementCommands.java:59 takes amount = number(p,"amount") with no sign or zero check, and the V27 Adjustments CHECK has no amount constraint. SettlementQueries.java:19 requires quantityDifference.signum() == 0 for SATISFIED. T19 itself separates the 5 BOX quantity difference from the 5 EUR amount difference.
confirmed.fix: Use one settlement predicate for closure and query. Require quantityDifference == 0 (or an explicit quantity-reconciliation fact) before resolution; otherwise only the typed MANAGER waiver may close. Reject zero-amount adjustments.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked this at 6fa7beb1 using git show, because the main checkout HEAD is the older 48d616e3. The core defect is real and reachable, but parts of the narrative overstate it.

Confirmed:
1. SettlementCommands.match (line 53) gives a match DIFFERENCE status when quantityDifference (qd), priceDifference (pd), currencyDifference, scopeDifference or originalDifference is nonzero. It computes originalDifference as invoiceAmount - min(received, ordered) * linePrice.
   - Scenario (a): invoice 50 BOX at 2 EUR against receipt 100 BOX at 1 EUR. qd=-50, pd=1, originalDifference=0, so the match is DIFFERENCE with a SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty.
2. SettlementResponsibilities.requireResolution (lines 25-30) requires a CONFIRMED adjustment of that exact match with an approver. It refuses only currencyDifference and scopeDifference, then requires remaining(match)==0. It never looks at quantityDifference or priceDifference.
   - In (a), remaining is already 0 before any adjustment. So a CONFIRMED 0 EUR adjustment is enough to resolve the duty.
3. Nothing blocks a zero adjustment:
   - SettlementCommands line 59 uses amount=number(p,"amount"), which has no sign or zero check.
   - The V27 Adjustments DDL (lines 85-100 and 150) has no CHECK on amount.
4. ResponsibilityCommands line 56 lets resolveObligation through because the catalog marks the kind resolvable. ResponsibilityService.settle (line 68) then sets the duty to RESOLVED.
5. The SATISFIED predicate in SettlementQueries line 19 additionally requires quantityDifference==0. So in T19's quantity branch (105 BOX at 1 EUR vs receipt 100), confirming a 5 EUR adjustment resolves the duty while getSettlement keeps reporting UNSATISFIED. The closure predicate and the query predicate disagree.
6. The asymmetry looks like an oversight. Currency and scope differences are explicitly kept out of amount-only closure, while quantity, which an amount adjustment equally cannot reconcile, is not.
7. Plan §5.3 (line 167) says resolveObligation must verify the duty's fulfilment evidence and that waivers go through the per-kind authority. A 0 EUR adjustment is not fulfilment evidence for a 50 BOX mismatch. In effect it is a waiver recorded as a verified resolution.
8. Test coverage:
   - The only backend test, SettlementCommandPostgresTest.exactManagerConfirmationRetainsOriginalVarianceAndDuty, covers a pure price difference (100 BOX at 1.05 EUR, qd=0).
   - T19 asserts that the quantity-difference duty is open and that confirmation is not resolution, but it never resolves that duty.
   - So the wrong behaviour passes every test.

Overstated parts:
- It is not an authorization bypass. CONFIRM requires a HUMAN actor with an active recordSettlementAdjustment ManagementAuthority. The plan §7 table (line 229) assigns "정산 차이 확정" (confirming a settlement difference) to MANAGER confirmation, and decideQuantityDutyWaiver is also MANAGER-class. A legitimately authorized human makes the decision; only its classification (resolve vs waive) and its evidentiary meaning are wrong.
- "50 boxes stay un-invoiced" overstates the effect. Match accounting sums prior quantities per line, reference and invoiceKind, so a later invoice can still bill the other 50.
- The "UNSATISFIED forever with no open duty" outcome in (b) also follows from the legitimate MANAGER waiver path. The query treats a quantity difference as permanently unsatisfied whatever the closure. That symptom is a query-model inconsistency, not something this resolver alone causes.

Net: the resolution evidence is weak and misleading, and the closure and query predicates are inconsistent. There is no data corruption and no privilege escalation. P2 stands.

confirmed.title: Adjustments confirmed after closure, or on MATCHED invoices, create ownerless settlement differences
confirmed.failure_scenario: Case 1: after the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty is RESOLVED (remaining 0) or WAIVED, a new adjustment of 3 EUR is proposed and confirmed. remaining becomes -3, getSettlement returns UNSATISFIED with settlementDifference -3, and the only duty is closed. Case 2: on a MATCHED invoice (dutyRootId null), confirming any non-zero adjustment turns the settlement UNSATISFIED with no duty at all. Either way the E1 requirement that unresolved settlement duties and their owners can be queried is lost.
confirmed.evidence: adjustment() (SettlementCommands.java:59-61) checks only match existence, currency, proposal hash and policy. It does not check the match status or the duty's state, and never calls impact.recorded. SettlementQueries.java:19 recomputes remaining from all CONFIRMED adjustments. The V29 invariant 'every DIFFERENCE keeps its human duty' (V29__settlement_scope_difference.sql) covers only Match.status, not adjustment-induced differences.
confirmed.fix: Reject adjustments on MATCHED matches or when the root duty is not OPEN. Alternatively, open (or keep open) a SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty keyed to the adjustment whenever remaining becomes non-zero.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The failure scenario is reachable at commit 6fa7beb1. I read the files with git show because the working tree is on a different commit.

How the code allows it:
- adjustment() in SettlementCommands.java:59-60 has six checks:
  - mode is PROPOSE or CONFIRM.
  - a Match exists for the invoice. It takes the first one and never looks at its status.
  - the match is not marked currencyDifference.
  - the adjustment currency equals the invoice currency.
  - a canonical SETTLEMENT_ADJUSTMENT occurrence exists.
  - for CONFIRM only: a human with active recordSettlementAdjustment authority, a matching proposal hash, no earlier confirmation, and the same policyVersion.
- No check looks at Match.status or at whether the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty (match.dutyRootId) is still OPEN. impact.recorded is never called on this path.
- The amount is signed: number() is used, not nonnegative().

Nothing else blocks it:
- TradeEvidence.requireCanonical (TradeEvidence.java:21-45) checks only kind, item, subject, quantity, verification and supersession.
- CommandPreparation does no duty-state gating.
- The DB adds nothing either. V27 Adjustments constraints cover only the mode/status/proposal shape, FKs and immutability. V29's CHECK ties dutyRootId only to Match.status, and Match rows are immutable. No constraint links adjustments to match status or duty state.
- Nothing reopens a resolved duty. grep finds no reopen logic. SettlementResponsibilities.requireResolution (lines 19-31) checks remaining==0 only once, at resolve time.

Reachable scenario:
1. An invoice is 5 EUR over. Match is DIFFERENCE and a SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty is OPEN.
2. A 5 EUR proposal is confirmed and the duty resolves (remaining 0). The test exactManagerConfirmationRetainsOriginalVarianceAndDuty stops here.
3. A second proposal for 5 EUR is then confirmed by the MANAGER. It could be a stale duplicate on a separate evidence occurrence, which is allowed: occurrenceId is unique but proposalHash is not.
4. remaining() and SettlementQueries.java:19 now give settlementDifference -5 and result UNSATISFIED, while the only duty is RESOLVED. No open settlement duty or owner exists.

The MATCHED case works the same way. originalDifference is 0, dutyRootId is null, and any confirmed non-zero adjustment makes getSettlement UNSATISFIED with no duty at all.

No test covers adjusting after resolution or on a MATCHED match. SettlementCommandPostgresTest.java:140-148 ends right after resolution.

Corrections to the claim:
- The WAIVED variant is weak. A waived duty already leaves remaining non-zero by design.
- "E1 lost" is overstated. The E1 fixture itself has no post-resolution adjustment, so E1 still passes.
- What is actually broken is the plan §6 rule (line 212, "정산 차이는 별도 미해결 목표다"): every unresolved settlement difference should stay an open goal with an owner, as D19/E1 expect.

Why P2: it takes a deliberate, authorized MANAGER confirmation. There is no authorization bypass and no ledger corruption. But it is a real gap in the invariant, and tests miss it. P2 is appropriate.

confirmed.title: The FX snapshot in the source original is silently dropped when the caller omits the fxSnapshot slot
confirmed.failure_scenario: The source invoice original contains fxSnapshot {EUR/KRW, 1500, ...}. The caller calls recordInvoice without the fxSnapshot slot. requireFields compares only line/amount/source keys, so the invoice is recorded with null fxPair/fxRate/convertedAmount. The canonical INVOICE review then passes because SettlementEvidence skips FX checks when invoice.fxPair is null. The plan-required conversion snapshot (pair/rate/date/source/policy and converted amount) is permanently lost. The test covers only the case where both carry or both omit the snapshot.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:48 runs the FX check only under `if(p.containsKey("fxSnapshot"))`. The expected map at line 46 omits fxSnapshot. SettlementEvidence.java:23 checks FX only when `invoice.get("fxPair")!=null`. Plan §6 정산 says 환율은 pair/rate/date/source/policy snapshot, 금액은 원통화/원금/환산값을 함께 보존. D19 requires the EUR/conversion snapshot.
confirmed.fix: Require slot/original parity both ways. If the original has fxSnapshot, the slot must be present and equal, and the reverse. Include fxSnapshot presence in the canonical review's expected fields.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this claim. I checked it against 6fa7beb1, where the cited lines match the current tree.

How the failure happens:
- At SettlementCommands.java:46 the `expected` map passed to `requireFields(source, expected)` covers line, reference, scope, kind, item, quantity, unit, unitPrice, originalAmount, currency and the source keys. It does not include fxSnapshot.
- `requireFields` (line 71) only checks that the expected keys match. Extra fields in the original, such as fxSnapshot, are ignored.
- Line 48 copies FX into the row only when the caller sends the slot: `if(p.containsKey("fxSnapshot"))`. The check only runs one way. A slot without FX in the original is held, but FX in the original without a slot is accepted.
- So an original carrying `fxSnapshot {EUR/KRW,1500,...}` plus a request with no fxSnapshot slot produces an Invoices row where all fx* columns and convertedAmount are null.

Nothing else blocks it:
- The DB constraint `settlement_fx_snapshot` (V27__settlement.sql:134) explicitly allows every FX column to be null.
- The capability contract (contracts/acceptance-capabilities.json) has no slot schema for recordInvoice.
- The gateway does not enforce required slots.
- In the canonical INVOICE review, SettlementEvidence.java:23 checks FX only when `invoice.fxPair != null`. With a null fxPair it also ignores the fxSnapshot in the payload and the original, so the review reports MATCHED.

Re-recording does not fix it later. The duplicate guard at line 45 (same namespace/key/version and same hash) rejects a second attempt with INVOICE_ALREADY_RECORDED, so the invoice record cannot get its FX snapshot for that source version.

Tests do not cover this case:
- SettlementCommandPostgresTest.prepareInvoice sends FX in both the original and the slot.
- realReceipt removes FX from both.
- The T19 native fixtures (fx-commercial, fx-correction and others) always send the fxSnapshot slot.

This conflicts with plan §6 정산 ("환율은 pair/rate/date/source/policy snapshot, 금액은 원통화/원금/환산값을 함께 보존한다"), with D19 (EUR/환산 snapshot), and with the class's own claim of "Exact original-to-claim proof".

Why I kept P2 and did not raise it:
- The original document stays in the evidence blob, so the claim's word "permanently lost" is overstated. What is lost is the snapshot on the invoice record and the converted value in settlement reads.
- matchInvoice decides using original-currency amounts only (it flags currencyDifference and does no conversion), so no quantity or money decision is corrupted.
- The trigger is a caller leaving out a slot, not an authorization bypass.

So this is a real but weakly enforced plan requirement with no test coverage. P2 is appropriate.

confirmed.title: CREDIT_NOTE/CORRECTION invoices get no persisted review duty and are invisible on the original invoice
confirmed.failure_scenario: A MATCHED/SATISFIED commercial invoice I (100 EUR) later receives a supplier CREDIT_NOTE of -5 with relatedInvoiceId I. recordInvoice APPLIES it and opens no duty. matchInvoice returns HELD SETTLEMENT_CORRECTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED with no effects, so nothing is persisted. getSettlement(I) still says SATISFIED and does not list the credit note. The 'human must review' requirement exists only as a transient error code with no owner, nextAction or nextCheck. relatedInvoiceId is optional, so orphan credit notes are also accepted.
confirmed.evidence: invoice() (lines 44-50) never calls impact.recorded. match() (line 52) throws HELD for correction kinds without persisting anything. SettlementQueries.java:18 `related()` selects only rows whose invoiceId equals the queried invoice and ignores Invoices.relatedInvoiceId. SettlementCommandPostgresTest.correctionInvoiceIsHeldForHumanReviewWithoutNewFulfillment asserts 0 SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duties.
confirmed.fix: Make relatedInvoiceId mandatory. When a CREDIT_NOTE/CORRECTION is recorded, open a review duty (owner and nextAction) on the original invoice's work in the same transaction, and show linked corrections, with result UNVERIFIED, in the original's getSettlement.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim holds at 6fa7beb1. No other guard, trigger or reader covers the gap.

1. **Recording a credit note opens no duty.** `SettlementCommands.invoice()` (lines 44-50) validates the credit note, links it through `relatedInvoiceId` only when the caller supplies it (line 49, so it is optional and orphan credit notes are accepted), inserts the row and returns APPLIED. It never calls `impact.recorded`.

2. **Matching it persists nothing.** `match()` (line 52) throws HELD `SETTLEMENT_CORRECTION_REVIEW_REQUIRED` for CREDIT_NOTE/CORRECTION. In `ApplicationCommands.java` (lines 82-83) and `CommandRepository.java` (line 31), HELD rolls back and is logged only as a REJECTED command record. V29 also rejects a Match INSERT for these kinds.

3. **No other path reaches it.** No other capability (such as a review or resolve-correction command) can act on a credit note, so it is a dead end with no owner, nextAction or nextCheck.

4. **The original invoice is unaffected.** `SettlementQueries.related()` (line 17) reads only Matches, Adjustments, Charges and PaymentReferences rows whose invoiceId equals the queried invoice. Outside the settlement package, nothing in `backend/src` or the migrations reads Invoices, so no work-closure check or operations list sees an unmatched credit note either. getSettlement(I) for a MATCHED invoice therefore still reports SATISFIED and does not list the credit note, even though the net billed amount now differs from the expected amount.

5. **The test locks this behaviour in.** `SettlementCommandPostgresTest.correctionInvoiceIsHeldForHumanReviewWithoutNewFulfillment` asserts APPLIED, then HELD, then 0 SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duties. The s4c README states that a human must review the credit note, but nothing records who or when.

**Why this matters against the plan:**
- §4.3 requires a correction to re-evaluate the affected judgments and duties in the same unit.
- §6 says a settlement difference is a separate unresolved goal and must not be erased.
- The intake rules leave unresolved items with an owner and nextCheck.

**Why not P1:**
- The plan never explicitly specifies credit-note semantics. T19 covers CREDIT_NOTE only for the FX snapshot.
- E1's "invoice difference 5" can be met through a COMMERCIAL invoice difference, which does create a duty.
- Losing the human-review responsibility without a trace is a real semantic defect, so P2 stands.

**Minor inaccuracies that do not change the verdict:**
- The scenario's "-5" is impossible, because amounts must be nonnegative (the V27 CHECK). The credit note is recorded as a positive 5.
- `related()` is at line 17, not 18.

confirmed.title: Every matched invoice records INVOICED, so duplicate and DOMESTIC_TAX invoices double-count invoiced quantity and block sales revision
confirmed.failure_scenario: A domestic sale line of 100 is delivered 100. Both the COMMERCIAL invoice and the DOMESTIC_TAX 세금계산서 for the same delivery are matched, which is allowed because overlap is per invoiceKind. A duplicate commercial invoice flagged scopeDifference would also count. Each match calls facts.invoiced, giving INVOICED = 200 for the line. SalesCommands.executed returns the max over kinds, 200, and reviseSalesOrder for any quantity below 200 (even a due-date-only change at 100) is HELD SALES_EXECUTION_PRESERVED. Purchase-side executed() similarly reports 200 invoiced.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:57 calls facts.invoiced(c,sk,line,iid,iq,unit) for every match regardless of invoiceKind or overlap. SalesCommands.java:33 sums by kind and takes the max; SalesCommands.java:23 HELDs when the new quantity < committed. PurchaseCommands.java:79 does the same sum and max. The s4c-settlement README (lines 94-95) acknowledges the risk 'if purchase/sales start using INVOICED sums', and those consumers already exist.
confirmed.fix: Do not record INVOICED execution for DOMESTIC_TAX (reference-only) or scopeDifference matches. Alternatively, record INVOICED per (line, reference) capped by the recognized contribution.

verdict.reasoning:
I could not refute this. The defect is reachable, and nothing in the code, the database or the tests neutralizes it.

1. **Every match records INVOICED.** `SettlementCommands.match` (line 57) calls `facts.invoiced(c,sk,line,iid,iq,unit)` unconditionally. The only invoice kinds it refuses to match are CREDIT_NOTE and CORRECTION (line 52), so DOMESTIC_TAX matches go through. Overlap is computed per invoiceKind (line 53), and the s4c-settlement README (line 24) says COMMERCIAL and DOMESTIC_TAX are deliberately not counted as duplicates of each other. A second COMMERCIAL invoice on the same delivery is also matched: it is only flagged `scopeDifference`/DIFFERENCE, and INVOICED is still recorded.

2. **Each invoice gets its own row.** `SettlementFactsAdapter.invoiced` (lines 40-42) writes an ExecutionEffect whose referenceId is the invoice ID. The dedupe in `SalesCommands.recordExecutionEffect` and `PurchaseCommands.recordExecutionEffect` is keyed on (line, kind, reference), so two invoices produce two rows. The recorded quantity is the full invoice quantity `iq`, not the matched quantity `min(received, ordered, iq)`. The database does not stop this either: V23 and V16 have only `CHECK(quantity>0)`, an immutability trigger and, on the purchase side, a unique index on (line, kind, referenceId). Nothing caps the sum.

3. **The inflated sum is consumed.**
   - `SalesCommands.executed` sums each kind across the revision ancestry and takes the maximum. `reviseSalesOrder` returns HELD `SALES_EXECUTION_PRESERVED` when the new quantity is below that value.
   - Concrete case: a sale line of 100, 40 delivered (DISPATCHED 40, DELIVERED 40). A COMMERCIAL invoice of 40 and a DOMESTIC_TAX invoice of 40 are both matched, so INVOICED = 80. Revising the order to 60 is HELD, although only 40 has been executed.
   - The allocation guard does not intervene: it only blocks EXECUTABLE or SUSPENDED allocations, and dispatched allocations are CONSUMED.
   - Purchase side: `cancelPurchase` uses the same max-of-sums. For a purchase with no shipment (so no SHIPPED effect, and therefore no `EXECUTION_OVERLAP_UNVERIFIED` hold), the same 40+40 invoices make cancelling the remaining 60 fail with "Cancellation cannot erase…", although the correct check would allow it. Where a SHIPPED effect also exists, that overlap guard returns HELD anyway, so the claim's purchase-side point is weaker there.

4. **No test covers it.** No test exercises a SALE-scope duplicate or DOMESTIC_TAX match followed by a revision or cancellation. The README lists "SALE scope 중복 송장의 실제 PG 사례" as NOT_RUN, and lines 94-95 explicitly leave the INVOICED-sum consumers unresolved, even though `SalesCommands.executed` and `PurchaseCommands.executed` already read that sum.

**Severity: P2 is right.** The INVOICED quantity really is double-counted. However, the failure only wrongly blocks legitimate revisions and cancellations (HELD or REJECTED). It does not let a wrong state commit or corrupt stock or settlement amounts, so P1/P0 would overstate it.

confirmed.title: Adjustments can be proposed/confirmed after the duty is RESOLVED, leaving a non-zero settlement difference with no open duty (duty vanishes, cannot be re-created)
confirmed.failure_scenario: Match originalDifference=5. MANAGER confirms adjustment 5 -> remaining 0 -> resolveObligation RESOLVES the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty. Later a second PROPOSE+CONFIRM of 5 (different canonical occurrences, legitimately verified) is accepted: adjustment() never looks at the duty state or current remaining. remaining() is now -5, getSettlement.result flips back to UNSATISFIED, but the only duty is RESOLVED and nothing re-opens one (match() is the only creator, matches are unique per invoice, adjustments/matches are immutable by trigger). The settlement is permanently inconsistent with zero human responsibility; 'duty non-revival' is correct, but the product silently manufactures a new unowned difference.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:59-62 adjustment(): only checks mode, match existence, currencyDifference, currency equality, proof, hash; no check on remaining() or on the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE assignment status. remaining() at line 63 sums all CONFIRMED adjustments unconditionally. V27 triggers settlement_adjustment_immutable / settlement_match_immutable prevent any later correction of the rows.
confirmed.fix: In adjustment(): when mode=CONFIRM (or PROPOSE), require that the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty for this match is still OPEN, or reject when the confirmed sum would overshoot (|remaining-amount| > |remaining| i.e. the adjustment moves remaining away from zero after it reached zero). Alternatively, when a confirmed adjustment makes remaining != 0 again, open a new SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty via impact.recorded with a new source command so the difference always has an owner.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked the claim against commit 6fa7beb1 and could not refute it. The failure scenario is reachable.

1. SettlementCommands.adjustment() (SettlementCommands.java:59-61) checks only these things: the mode is PROPOSE or CONFIRM, a match exists, there is no currencyDifference, the adjustment currency equals the invoice currency, the canonical proof and original-document fields match, and for CONFIRM the manager authority, proposal hash, not-already-confirmed status and policy version. It does not read remaining(), the match status (MATCHED or DIFFERENCE), or the state of the SETTLEMENT_DIFFERENCE duty.
2. The proposal hash covers only invoiceId, matchId, amount, currency and reason. It does not bind the remaining difference at proposal time. The gateway's currentRevision is the invoice revision, and invoices are immutable (constant revision 1), so nothing makes a stale proposal fail. Plan §7 (line 235: approvals store the target revision, and changed effects need re-review) is therefore not enforced here.
3. TradeEvidence.requireCanonical (TradeEvidence.java:21-50) validates only the evidence chain and never looks at duty state. The DB schema (V27__settlement.sql:145-158) has unique(occurrenceId), a unique confirmation per proposalId, a mode/status CHECK and immutability triggers. None of these limit the cumulative confirmed amount.
4. SettlementResponsibilities.requireResolution (SettlementResponsibilities.java:19-31) checks remaining()==0 only at the moment of resolution. Nothing in main code reopens a RESOLVED duty or creates a new one. The only creator is impact.recorded in match() (line 56), and the Matches unique(organizationId, invoiceId) constraint allows only one match per invoice.
5. Negative amounts are accepted (SettlementInputs.number has no sign check), so a later corrective -5 adjustment could bring remaining back to 0. Even so, while the -5 difference exists it has no owner or open duty. getSettlement (SettlementQueries.java:19) reports result=UNSATISFIED with settlementDifference -5, which contradicts plan §6 정산 ("정산 차이는 별도 미해결 목표") and the E1 expectation that every unresolved settlement difference has an obligation and owner.

Concrete path: match originalDifference=5 → PROPOSE P1 of 5 and P2 of 5, each with its own verified canonical SETTLEMENT_ADJUSTMENT occurrence → MANAGER confirms P1 → resolveObligation succeeds (the duty becomes RESOLVED) → MANAGER confirms P2. Every check in steps 1-3 passes. remaining becomes -5 and no open duty exists. The same happens if P2 is proposed after resolution.

There is an even simpler variant the claim does not mention: on a match with status MATCHED (diff 0, so no duty is ever created), any PROPOSE+CONFIRM of a nonzero amount is accepted and produces an UNSATISFIED settlement with no duty at all.

Test coverage: SettlementCommandPostgresTest.exactManagerConfirmationRetainsOriginalVarianceAndDuty (lines 140-150) covers only a single exact adjustment followed by resolution. No test confirms an adjustment after resolution or on a MATCHED match.

Why P2 and not higher: the scenario needs a MANAGER to deliberately confirm a redundant or over-correcting proposal. The command output shows settlementDifference -5. There is no bank or tax effect, recorded history is not mutated, and quantities are unaffected. So this is a gap in the invariant "an unsatisfied settlement has an open owned duty", plus a stale-approval gap. It does not corrupt data or bypass authorization.

confirmed.title: PURCHASE-scope matchInvoice reconciles against the stored ReceiptCredit quantity without re-verifying that the receipt canonical occurrence is still current (SALE path does); a superseded receipt fact can be matched as MATCHED
confirmed.failure_scenario: Receipt canonical occurrence R1 (100 BOX) is credited to PO line L (ReceiptCredits.actualQuantity=100). The evidence layer later records a verified corrected canonical occurrence R2 with supersedesId=R1 (quantity 80); the purchase domain has no receipt-correction port, so the credit row stays at 100. A supplier invoice for 100 is matched: contribution() returns the credit row verbatim (quantity=100, occurrenceId=R1); match() calls proof()/requireCanonical only for the INVOICE occurrence, never for the receipt occurrence, so Matches.occurrenceId=R1 (superseded) and status=MATCHED. For SALE scope the same step goes through DeliveryCorrection.deliveryCredit, which re-verifies the current PHYSICAL_DELIVERY canonical, so the two scopes behave differently. The invoice is reconciled against quantity the system itself no longer considers the current fact.
confirmed.evidence: SettlementFactsAdapter.java:36-38 `var credit=purchase.receiptCredit(c,lineId,referenceId);return Map.of("quantity",credit.get("actualQuantity"),...)`; PurchaseCommands.java:75 receiptCredit() returns the stored row with only a knownAt filter; SettlementCommands.java:53 `var contribution=facts.contribution(...);BigDecimal received=positive(contribution.get("quantity"))` with proof() only for kind INVOICE (line 72). Contrast DeliveryCorrection.java:14 `verified.requireCanonical(c,canonical,"PHYSICAL_DELIVERY",...)` for SALE. grep shows no ReceiptCorrections/correctReceipt anywhere in backend/src/main or database/migrations.
confirmed.fix: In SettlementFactsAdapter.contribution (PURCHASE branch) or in SettlementCommands.match, call TradeEvidence.requireCanonical on contribution.occurrenceId with the credited quantity/unit (as the SALE path does) so a superseded or unverified receipt occurrence cannot be matched; document that a receipt-correction path for purchase is pending if that is the intended S5 scope.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked this against commit 6fa7beb1. Its trade and evidence code is identical to HEAD. The scenario as written can't happen, but a close variant can, and it produces the same wrong result. So I am not refuting the claim, and P2 stays.

**Why the stated scenario can't happen**
- The claim needs a corrected receipt occurrence R2 with supersedesId=R1. The only place that inserts CanonicalOccurrences is EvidenceRecords.java:132.
- The only CanonicalInput that sets a supersedesId comes from EvidenceReconciliation.link (line 187). It passes `correctionPrior`, and deliveryCorrectionPrior (line 145) returns null for any kind other than PHYSICAL_DELIVERY.
- For a receipt whose quantity changed from 100 to 80, link() finds R1 by physicalScopeId and effectiveFrom, sets existing=R1, and verifyCanonical then rejects the quantity difference ("Canonical occurrence mismatch"). The reconciliation match also returns CONFLICT. So a receipt never gets a superseding canonical occurrence.

**The variant that does happen**
1. R1 (PHYSICAL_RECEIPT, 100 BOX) is verified and credited to PO line L. creditReceipt (PurchaseCommands.java:76) checks requireCanonical at that point, so the ReceiptCredits row is valid when written.
2. Someone with the correctEvidence grant corrects R1's source Event, Claim or DocumentVersion. EvidenceRecordCommands routes this to recordActivity, recordClaim or attachDocument with supersedesId, and none of these restricts the kind.
3. R1 now has no current verification chain. TradeEvidence.java:45 skips the chain when its event, claim or document has been superseded, so requireCanonical(R1) throws HELD EVIDENCE_UNVERIFIED. As shown above, the corrected quantity can never become a current receipt fact.
4. A supplier invoice for 100 is recorded against L with receiptOccurrenceId=R1. recordInvoice does not check the reference.
5. matchInvoice calls SettlementFactsAdapter.contribution (lines 36–38). That returns the stored ReceiptCredits row from PurchaseCommands.receiptCredit (line 75), which filters only on knownAt. SettlementCommands.match (lines 53–57) calls proof()/requireCanonical only for the INVOICE occurrence.
6. The result is an immutable Match with occurrenceId=R1, receivedQuantity=100, status MATCHED and settlementResult SATISFIED. Because of the INVOICE_ALREADY_MATCHED guard, the invoice can never be matched again.

**Why this is a defect**
- The SALE scope blocks the same step. DeliveryCorrection.deliveryCredit (line 14) re-runs requireCanonical on the current PHYSICAL_DELIVERY occurrence.
- Plan §4.3 says that after a correction, follow-up commands are blocked until the needed confirmation (후속 명령은 필요한 확정까지 막는다). The PURCHASE path breaks that rule.
- No test covers this. SettlementCommandPostgresTest is the only test file that uses matchInvoice, and it never calls correctEvidence.

**What limits the severity**
- AssessmentCorrectionImpact still invalidates the affected Works and opens correction duties, so responsibility is not lost.
- Quantities are not double counted, and no stock or bank effect follows.
- The harm is a settlement recorded as SATISFIED against receipt evidence the system now treats as unverified, with no way to re-match it.

That is a real plan violation with a reachable path. It is not data corruption or an authorization bypass, so P2 fits.

**Fix:** the proposed fix still applies. Call TradeEvidence.requireCanonical on the PURCHASE contribution's occurrenceId, using the credit's actualQuantity, unit, item and physicalScopeId, before matching. Also document that purchase receipt-credit correction is not implemented yet.

unverifiedP3.title: Transfer and partial-split tests never exercise ResponsibilityService.transfer
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: transferDoesNotResolveGoalOrCloseSource only calls requireSettled on a mocked TRANSFERRED row; it never transfers. ResponsibilityPostgresTest (e.g. partialTransferConservesLeafAndAssignmentQuantityWithoutParentDoubleCount, line 29) simulates transfers with raw SQL UPDATEs. A broken transfer()/decide(TRANSFER) would pass all of these as long as DB triggers hold, for example a moving-range offset error, a remaining child assigned to the wrong work, or wrong nextAction/owner. Examples: the split computing [start, q) for the target, or the source remainder getting the target's owner.
unverifiedP3.evidence: No backend test calls transferObligation/acceptHandover with a TRANSFER handover (grep shows only binding and harness-assertion tests). ResponsibilityService.transfer (ResponsibilityService.java:40) has no direct coverage.

unverifiedP3.title: INVOICED execution effect records the full invoice quantity for overlapping DIFFERENCE matches and for DOMESTIC_TAX reference invoices, so a line's cumulative INVOICED effects can exceed received/ordered quantity
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: Receipt 100. COMMERCIAL invoice 100 matched (MATCHED, INVOICED 100). DOMESTIC_TAX invoice 100 for the same contribution is matched separately (prior filter is per invoiceKind, so not an overlap): INVOICED 100 recorded again. A second COMMERCIAL invoice 100 is matched: scopeDifference=true, DIFFERENCE, duty opened — but facts.invoiced still records INVOICED 100. ExecutionEffects now say 300 invoiced against 100 received. No reader of kind INVOICED exists today (grep), so it is latent, but the S4C README treats 'INVOICED 효과 0' as a meaningful contract and any future consumer (goal satisfaction, cancellation 'already executed range') would double count.
unverifiedP3.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:57 `r.insert("Matches",row);facts.invoiced(c,sk,line,iid,iq,unit);` executed unconditionally after status is computed; SettlementFactsAdapter.java:40-43 forwards to recordExecutionEffect(..,"INVOICED",invoiceId,q,unit); PurchaseCommands.java:77 / SalesCommands.java:32 dedupe only per (lineId,kind,referenceId=invoiceId). docs/execution/s4c-settlement/README.md:24-27 states INVOICED effects are part of the contract.
unverifiedP3.fix: Record the INVOICED effect with the non-overlapping matched quantity (quantity minus the overlap beyond received) or skip it when scopeDifference is true, and skip it for taxReferenceOnly invoices (DOMESTIC_TAX), so execution effects never exceed the recognized contribution. Add an assertion on SUM(ExecutionEffects.quantity WHERE kind='INVOICED') in the overlap test.

unverifiedP3.title: recordInvoice silently drops the FX snapshot present in the immutable original when the caller omits fxSnapshot, and a foreign-currency invoice does not require one
unverifiedP3.failure_scenario: The source document carries fxSnapshot {EUR/KRW 1500 ...} for a EUR invoice against a KRW line. The caller sends recordInvoice without the fxSnapshot slot. The invoice row is stored with all fx* columns NULL and convertedAmount NULL although the original attests a snapshot; getSettlement shows no 환산값. D19/§6 require 원통화/원금/환산값 to be preserved together; the current check is one-directional (caller-supplied snapshot must match the source, not vice versa). Only the positive path is tested (invoiceGatewayPreservesFx...).
unverifiedP3.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:48 `if(p.containsKey("fxSnapshot")){...}` — the branch is skipped entirely when the slot is absent; expected fields at line 46 do not include fxSnapshot. SettlementAmountsTest/SettlementCommandPostgresTest only cover a supplied snapshot.
unverifiedP3.fix: Treat the source's fxSnapshot as authoritative: if source.fxSnapshot is present, require the slot (or derive from the source) and store it; optionally require a snapshot whenever invoice currency != line currency. Add a negative test: source with snapshot + slot omitted -> HELD.

unverifiedP3.title: relatedInvoiceId of CREDIT_NOTE/CORRECTION invoices is optional and not attested by the immutable original; a correction can be bound to an arbitrary invoice of the same line or to none

unverifiedP3.evidence: SettlementCommands.java:49 `if(Set.of("CREDIT_NOTE","CORRECTION").contains(kind)&&p.containsKey("relatedInvoiceId")){...}` only checks line/scope equality; expected map at line 46 omits relatedInvoiceId; SettlementEvidence.require (line 23) also does not include it in the semantic hash.
